title: reg_code_blocks carries one count for both its size and its used entries, so a recursive compile writes into a reallocated array
live_proof: upstream fixed it in 40727c420c (40727c420c8e9ed61971dd46fc738132b9e4d5db) (2024-05-06). That commit is an ancestor of v5.45.3-85-gdb19522155 and is NOT an ancestor of the v5.36.3 tag (checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, both directions), so it never reached the 5.36 maintenance branch; the pin's tree shows the unfixed code (pin regexp.h:94 int count (one field for both size and used); regcomp.c:7291 dst = &pRExC_state->code_blocks->cb[n] with n reset per recursion). Host ASan at the pin: ASan: SEGV (rc=77); the same trigger, same harness and same ASan options on master: no report (rc=0, the harness reports [PASS])
fidelity: the trigger is the test upstream added with its own fix, extracted onto a self-contained harness that collects failures instead of aborting, so one script yields one verdict. It is upstream's own reproduction, not a reduction of ours; what it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it
status: all four Capstone arms measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM, each after passing its own two controls. cheribsd-revocation NOT measured: Perl 5.36.3 purecap faults in perl_construct when linked static, and the stock loader refuses the dynamic image (results/20261006-cheribsd-blocked)
allocator_layer: system allocator (the reg_code_block array, via Newx/Renew)
